_doc: Skeleton index — organized by families (argument type) with emphasis variants. The matcher reads this single file. Flow: intake fingerprint → match family → detect/ask emphasis → pick variant → load that variant's contract.

families.description: Diagnostic arc — names a problem, explains its root cause(s), proposes a fix

signals: prompt contains a problem/loss/cost/risk AND its cause/driver/reason AND an action/fix/recommendation
quantifiable negative impact
cause can be decomposed into 2-4 segments

cause_visual_options._doc: The cause zone uses swappable chart types. Each skeleton defaults to one; the builder matches based on data shape. No variant multiplication needed — the chart type is a contract-level decision.

segmented-bar.data_fit: composition — parts sum to 100%, proportional breakdown of a whole

ranked-bars.data_fit: magnitude — independent drivers ranked by absolute value, not parts of a whole

trend-bars.data_fit: temporal — cause is a worsening trend over time, shown as mini vertical bar chart

cause_visual_options.routing: If user's cause data sums to 100% → segmented-bar. If independent cost/magnitude items → ranked-bars. If temporal progression → trend-bars.

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'convince to act' or 'get approval' → decision. If 'understand why' or 'root cause' → cause. If 'how bad is it' or 'impact' → impact. If unclear → ask.

options.label: Balanced view
options.description: Equal weight across problem, cause, and fix

options.label: The financial impact
options.description: Lead with the cost — hero stat dominates, cause and fix are supporting

options.label: The root cause
options.description: Lead with the breakdown — cause analysis is the hero, flanked by problem and fix

options.label: The decision
options.description: Lead with the action options — what to do is the hero, problem and cause are context

variants.name: 3-column equal weight
variants.layout: 3 equal columns: problem | cause | fix. Each has hero stat + claim + detail content. Progression strip at bottom.

variants.name: Impact hero with cause/fix sidebar
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: 72px hero stat + claim + 2 supporting stats. Right: stacked cause (ranked horizontal bars by magnitude) + fix (action steps). Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Cause breakdown hero
variants.layout: Full-width cause segmented bar (36px) as hero in surface panel with aligned legend. Below: 2-column grid — left problem stat + context, right fix stat + action steps. Callout band at bottom.

variants.name: Decision-forward with context rail
variants.layout: Left 35%: context rail with problem stat + cause trend mini-chart (6-quarter vertical bars). Right 65%: 2 option zone-cards side by side, each with badge + title + metric + bullets. Decision callout at bottom.

families.description: Value walk — start → drivers (gains/drags) → end. Classic bridge or margin decomposition.

signals: prompt describes change from one value to another
names specific drivers/factors explaining the change
has start and end values with contributing items

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more about this walk?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on 'what drove the change' → drivers. If 'where we ended up' → outcome. If 'what went wrong' → drags.

options.label: Full bridge
options.description: Equal weight — start, all drivers, end shown proportionally

options.label: Driver deep-dive
options.description: Chart is hero, findings annotate the top 2-3 drivers

options.label: Outcome focus
options.description: End value is the hero stat, bridge is supporting context

variants.name: 60/40 waterfall + annotated findings
variants.layout: Left 60%: waterfall chart with labeled bars. Right 40%: 2-3 analyst findings with chips.

variants.name: Executive waterfall with action strip
variants.layout: Full-width waterfall chart as hero. Below: callout band + action progression strip.

families.description: Items ranked or composed by value — who's biggest, what's the mix, where's the concentration.

signals: prompt lists items with comparable values
natural ordering by magnitude
concentration or dominance pattern

emphasis_question.prompt: What's the story in the ranking?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user highlights a gap between top and rest → dominance. If distribution matters → spread. If comparing two groups → split.

options.label: Top-heavy
options.description: Lead item dominates — hero stat is the leader, bar chart shows the drop-off

options.label: Even spread
options.description: Distribution is the story — all items shown proportionally, no single hero

options.label: Two-group contrast
options.description: Top group vs bottom group — visual split emphasizes the divide

variants.name: Ranked bar chart + annotated rail
variants.layout: Left 55%: horizontal ranked bar chart with stats line. Right 45%: compact data table + findings rail with semantic chips. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Ranked bars with tier colors + spread annotations
variants.layout: Left 55%: horizontal ranked bar chart with semantic tier colors (high-cost/mid-range/low-cost) + vs-avg delta badges + spread summary line. Right 45%: compact data table with vs-avg column + findings rail with semantic chips. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Performance vs a reference point — industry benchmark, competitor, prior period, target.

signals: prompt compares values against a benchmark or reference
has 'vs', 'compared to', 'relative to', 'gap'
named reference entity (industry, competitor, target)

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more — where you stand or the gap?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user asks 'how do we compare' → position. If 'how far behind' or 'what to close' → gap.

options.label: Competitive position
options.description: Side-by-side comparison — reader sees relative standing

options.label: Gap to close
options.description: Delta is the hero — reader sees what needs to change

variants.name: Margin comparison with benchmark line
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: hero gap stat + horizontal bars with benchmark markers + gap badges. Right: findings with bridge text + action block. Consultant credibility sourcing.

families.description: Stages, phases, or steps in a sequence — pipeline, lifecycle, methodology, flywheel.

signals: prompt describes sequential stages or phases
has step 1/2/3 or phase language
describes a pipeline, workflow, or methodology

emphasis_question.prompt: Is this about the overall system or a specific bottleneck?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on one broken step → bottleneck. If describing the whole approach → system. If showing adoption → progress.

options.label: Full system view
options.description: All stages shown equally — reader sees the whole process

options.label: Bottleneck focus
options.description: One stage is called out — reader sees where it breaks

options.label: Progress tracking
options.description: Stages shown with done/current/next status

variants.name: Flywheel with thesis banner
variants.layout: Circular flywheel diagram with thesis banner above. Stage labels around the ring.

variants.name: Trend chart with KPI strip
variants.layout: Full-width stacked bar chart as hero. KPI stat-row below chart. Optional annotation marker.

variants.name: Pipeline funnel with bottleneck callout
variants.layout: Narrowing funnel diagram. Bottleneck stage highlighted. Findings annotate the drop-off.

families.description: New capability, product, or initiative — what it is, why it matters, what changes.

signals: prompt announces something new
has 'launching', 'introducing', 'new capability', 'rolling out'
describes what it does + why it matters

emphasis_question.prompt: What should land first — the product or the impact?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user wants to show the UI → product. If they want to argue for adoption → impact.

options.label: Product showcase
options.description: Screenshot/mockup is the hero — messaging supports it

options.label: Impact argument
options.description: Benefits are the hero — product visual is supporting

variants.name: Icon-text stack + product mockup
variants.layout: Left 46%: icon-text messaging blocks. Right 54%: product image placeholder. Callout band below.

families.description: Internal alignment — thesis, strategic pillars, goals, rationale. For team buy-in, not external audiences.

signals: prompt describes strategy, priorities, or pillars
has 'our approach', 'strategic priorities', 'key pillars'
internal audience, not client-facing

emphasis_question.prompt: Is this about the big picture or the specific priorities?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user wants alignment on direction → thesis. If listing specific workstreams → pillars.

options.label: Thesis-first
options.description: Lead with the overarching strategy, pillars support it

options.label: Pillar-first
options.description: Lead with the workstreams, thesis is context

variants.name: Thesis banner + strategy pillars
variants.layout: Goals banner with thesis statement. Below: side-by-side strategy pillar groups with numbered items.

variants.name: Two-zone drivers + evidence
variants.layout: Thesis formula card. Below: two-zone split — left has icon-text-stack drivers, right has evidence-group cards with line items and badges.

families.description: 1-slide proposal — business need, proposed solution, recommended approach. The slide that closes deals.

signals: prompt asks for an executive summary or 1-slide overview of an engagement
has 'business need', 'proposed solution', 'approach', 'executive summary'
three-part arc: what's wrong, what we'll do, how we'll do it

emphasis_question.prompt: What should land hardest?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user emphasizes the pain/cost → problem. If the solution design → solution. If the engagement model → approach. If equal weight → balanced.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: Need, solution, and approach shown side by side — reader follows the arc

options.label: The business pain
options.description: Problem metrics dominate — solution and approach are supporting

options.label: The solution design
options.description: Solution details are the hero — problem is context, approach is footer

options.label: The engagement model
options.description: Timeline and scope dominate — problem and solution are compact context

variants.name: Stat row + 3-column need/solution/approach
variants.layout: Context bar at top. Stat row (4 KPIs) as hero. Below: 3-column findings grid — Business Need | Proposed Solution | Recommended Approach. Action column in orange accent.

families.description: Side-by-side old state → new state with delta callouts. Proposals, restructured deals, timeline compression.

signals: prompt compares a previous/old/current state to a new/updated/proposed state
has 'before/after', 'previous vs updated', 'old → new', 'compressed', 'restructured'
quantifiable deltas between the two states (cost, time, scope)

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user emphasizes savings/reduction → savings. If restructured responsibilities → ownership. If equal weight → balanced.

options.label: Full comparison
options.description: Equal weight — both states shown with deltas between them

options.label: The savings
options.description: Delta callouts dominate — reader sees the improvement first

options.label: The new structure
options.description: After-state scope cards dominate — reader sees who owns what

variants.name: Decision story — comparison rows + narrative + ownership
variants.layout: Left 46%: comparison table (label | previous | delta | updated). Right 54%: narrative + process models + ownership split. Bottom: neutral hairline strip.

variants.name: Savings-hero with before/after context
variants.layout: Hero delta stats across top. Below: compact before/after comparison as supporting context.

variants.name: Ownership-forward with compact deltas
variants.layout: Large ownership cards as hero (60%). Compact before/after KPI strip and deltas as sidebar (40%).

families.description: Same starting point, materially different outcomes — the spread itself is the problem. Divergence diagram, scatter, or benchmark bars visualize the fan-out; narrative explains what's driving the variance.

signals: prompt has a single starting value/input that produces multiple different outcomes
variance or spread is not explained by the obvious variable (size, volume, tier)
entities can be compared on multiple dimensions (price, discount, margin)
the pattern suggests ad-hoc or inconsistent processes, not market forces

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user asks 'show the spread' or 'visualize the variance' → balanced. If 'how big is the gap' → spread. If 'what's causing it' → drivers.

options.label: Full diagnostic
options.description: Equal weight — visual shows the variance, narrative explains the drivers and fix

options.label: Spread is the hero
options.description: Gap magnitude dominates — visual is compact supporting context

options.label: Driver deep-dive
options.description: Expanded driver analysis is the hero — variance visual is compact sidebar

variants.name: Divergence flow + narrative findings
variants.layout: 52/48 split. Left: source orb → fork label → N outcome orbs with entity cards. Right: finding title + variance drivers + quote + action card with chips.

variants.name: Scatter chart + data table + findings rail
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: scatter plot (Y=discount, X=revenue) with labeled data points + compact data table. Right: 3 findings with semantic dots + stakeholder observations + action block.

variants.name: Benchmark bars with gap badges + findings
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: hero gap stat + two benchmark bar panels with gap annotations + interpretation line. Right: 3 detailed findings with bridge text + numbered action steps.

variants.name: Spread hero — full-width divergence flow with compact driver strip
variants.layout: Full-width divergence flow as hero (65% height). Larger orbs, spread callout bracket on right edge. Below: 2-column strip — left drivers (compact), right action card.

variants.name: Drivers hero — ranked bars with context rail
variants.layout: 38/62 split (inverted). Left context rail: compact source strip + outcome rows with mini orbs + spread badge. Right hero: finding title + ranked driver bars with magnitude + quote + action card.

families.description: Key findings from an assessment — 3-5 sourced findings, each with supporting data and a client bridge. The bread-and-butter consultant deliverable.

signals: prompt presents multiple findings or observations from an assessment/review
each finding has supporting data or evidence
no dominant visual (chart, diagram) — the structured findings ARE the deliverable
no dominant diagnostic arc — OR findings form a causal chain toward explicit actions (BECAUSE/BUT connectors → action items with owners)
prompt compares metrics against targets/benchmarks but the structured findings ARE the deliverable (not a benchmark chart)

emphasis_question.prompt: How should the findings be weighted?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the prompt has 3+ explicit action items with owners/timelines → action-forward. If the user highlights one dominant finding → hero-finding. If the user emphasizes what to do about it → action-forward. If all findings are equally important → balanced.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: All findings shown equally in a grid — reader scans the full picture

options.label: Lead finding
options.description: One key finding is elevated as the hero — the rest support it

options.label: Action-forward
options.description: Findings are compact context — the recommendation block dominates

variants.name: KPI strip + 3-column bullet findings
variants.layout: Claim headline. Stat-row (3 KPIs). 3-column bullet findings (title + 2-3 bullets + source). Implication-strip action band. Footer.

variants.name: 3-row findings exhibit with hero-stat evidence
variants.layout: Full-width 3-column exhibit grid (Finding 22% | Evidence 42% | Implication 36%). 3 numbered rows with hero-stat evidence (large value + descriptor + detail + source) and highlighted implication panels. Callout band at bottom.

variants.name: Two-zone narrative findings + dominant action steps
variants.layout: Two-zone split. Left ~25%: narrative findings strip (3 stat pods stacked vertically with BECAUSE/BUT connectors). Right ~75%: action claim title + 3 horizontal methodology step cards (icon + title + desc + owner/timeline) + callout band.

families.description: Capability scoring against a maturity model — where you are, where peers are, what's dragging the score down. The classic 'you're at level 2 of 5' consultant deliverable.

signals: prompt scores capabilities against a maturity model or readiness scale
has 'maturity', 'readiness', 'capability assessment', 'score X out of Y', 'level'
compares current state to a target or peer benchmark on a defined scale

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user asks 'where do we stand' → position. If 'what's holding us back' → gaps. If 'what do we do about it' → action.

options.label: Current position
options.description: Maturity track is the hero — reader sees where they sit on the scale

options.label: Capability gaps
options.description: Capability breakdown bars are the hero — reader sees which dimensions drag the score

options.label: Closing the gap
options.description: Action plan dominates — maturity track and scores are compact context

variants.name: Maturity track + capability bars + findings
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: maturity stage track (5 stages, current + target highlighted) with gap badge, capability score bars below. Right: 3 findings + action block.

variants.name: Capability bars hero with compact maturity rail
variants.layout: Full-width capability bar chart as hero (ranked worst-first, target lines). Compact maturity stage strip above. Findings + action below.

variants.name: Action roadmap with compact maturity context
variants.layout: Left 40%: compact maturity track + overall score + capability sparklines. Right 60%: sequenced action cards (3-4 steps) with target score and priority rationale.

families.description: Quick-reference data — rate cards, fee schedules, conversion tables, policy parameters. Not argumentative; the data IS the deliverable, with rationale as context.

signals: prompt presents a table of reference values (rates, fees, thresholds, parameters)
has 'rate card', 'fee schedule', 'conversion table', 'reference', 'fixed rates', 'lookup'
reader needs to find a specific value quickly, not follow a narrative

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more — the data or why it's set this way?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user just needs the numbers → data. If they need to explain the methodology → rationale. If one row is the key decision → highlight.

options.label: Data-first
options.description: Table dominates — rationale is a sidebar for context

options.label: Rationale-first
options.description: Equal weight — table and methodology shown side by side

options.label: Key-row callout
options.description: One row or value is the hero — the rest of the table is supporting context

variants.name: Data table + rationale sidebar
variants.layout: 50/50 split. Left: styled data table with header row, base-row highlight, footnote. Right: rationale header + 3-4 rationale items. Action band at bottom.

variants.name: Methodology-forward with compact table
variants.layout: Left 55%: methodology title + 4 rationale cards with icons. Right 45%: compact data table. Callout band at bottom.

families.description: Performance tracked over time periods — quarterly revenue, monthly pipeline, annual headcount. The story is in the trajectory and mix shift, not a single delta.

signals: prompt has values for the same metric across 3+ time periods
has 'quarterly', 'monthly', 'Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4', 'year-over-year', 'trend'
multiple series or categories tracked over the same time axis

emphasis_question.prompt: What's the story in the trend?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user highlights one series growing or shrinking → focal-series. If the overall mix is shifting → mix-shift. If just showing the trajectory → trajectory.

options.label: Full trajectory
options.description: Stacked chart + data table — reader sees all series over all periods

options.label: One series stands out
options.description: Chart highlights the focal series — hero stat + findings explain why it matters

options.label: Mix is shifting
options.description: Composition change is the story — share percentages and mix-shift callouts dominate

variants.name: Stacked bar chart + data table + findings rail
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: stacked bar chart (4 series × 4 periods) with legend + KPI strip above. Right: compact data table with Δ column + 3-4 findings with semantic chips. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Focal series hero with contribution context
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: stacked bar chart with focal series highlighted (no per-segment labels). Right: lead-stat hero (focal growth) + mix-shift context + 2 narrative findings + callout band. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: What drove the change — contribution bars showing which categories added or subtracted from a total. The bridge endpoints are bookends; the drivers are the story.

signals: prompt names a total that grew or shrank and lists what contributed
has 'contributed', 'drove growth', 'offset by', 'net change', 'added/subtracted'
categories have positive and negative contributions that sum to a net delta

emphasis_question.prompt: What should land first — the drivers or the headline number?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on the biggest contributor → driver-hero. If the total change is the headline → headline-hero. If showing the full decomposition → balanced.

options.label: Full decomposition
options.description: Bridge endpoints + contribution bars + narrative — reader traces the whole walk

options.label: Lead driver
options.description: Biggest contributor is the hero stat — chart and narrative support it

options.label: Headline number
options.description: Net change is the hero — contribution bars are supporting context

variants.name: Bridge endpoints + contribution bars + narrative
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: bridge panel (start → end with delta) + diverging contribution bars (positive right, negative left) with net total. Right: hero stat + mix-shift + narrative + callout band.

variants.name: Lead driver callout with compact decomposition
variants.layout: Left 40%: hero stat (lead driver) + mix-shift badge + narrative. Right 60%: compact bridge + contribution bars. Summary band at bottom.

variants.name: Net change hero with supporting decomposition
variants.layout: Left 45%: hero stat (net change) + trend context + narrative. Right 55%: compact bridge + contribution bars + net total. The total is the story; drivers are proof.

families.description: Two parallel workstreams tracked side by side — internal readiness vs client adoption, build vs rollout, training vs deployment. Each track has its own milestones and KPIs.

signals: prompt tracks two distinct but related workstreams in parallel
has 'track 1 / track 2', 'internal + external', 'build + adopt', 'readiness + deployment'
each track has its own completion metric or milestone status

emphasis_question.prompt: Are the two tracks equally important, or is one the bottleneck?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If one track is done and the other is the focus → handoff. If both tracks need equal attention → parallel. If showing the overall program → program.

options.label: Two equal tracks
options.description: Both tracks shown side by side with matching visual weight

options.label: Handoff moment
options.description: Track A is done — the slide is about transitioning focus to Track B

options.label: Program overview
options.description: Both tracks feed a shared objective — the goal card is the hero

variants.name: Side-by-side track panels with KPI chips
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with thesis. Two side-by-side section panels. Left: journey timeline (done/current/target nodes) + audience grid + enablement cards. Right: adoption list + objective card. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Completed track compact + active track hero
variants.layout: Left 35%: compact completed-track summary (check badges + stat). Right 65%: active track as hero — timeline, current items, next actions. Goal card at bottom.

variants.name: Shared goal hero with compact track strips
variants.layout: Hero goal card at top (40%). Below: two compact track strips side by side showing milestone status + KPI. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Four-category landscape map — 2×2 grid of named categories, each with icon-text items. For channel strategies, capability maps, stakeholder groupings, resource allocation by bucket.

signals: prompt organizes items into 3-4 named categories or buckets
has 'categories', 'channels', 'quadrants', 'pillars', 'groups', 'buckets'
items partition a landscape — distinct categories, not sequential phases
no dominant visual (chart, timeline) — the categorization IS the deliverable

emphasis_question.prompt: How should the four categories relate to each other?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user just wants a clean map → balanced. If one category is more important → focal. If there's a top-row vs bottom-row distinction → paired.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: All four categories shown at the same scale — reader scans the full landscape

options.label: One category leads
options.description: One quadrant is expanded as the hero — the other three are compact context

options.label: Paired rows
options.description: Top row vs bottom row has a narrative distinction (e.g. proven vs experimental)

variants.name: Headline + 2×2 quadrant grid with icon items
variants.layout: 32/68 split. Left: claim headline zone (vertically centered). Right: 2×2 grid — each quadrant has colored pill header + 3 icon-text items. Horizontal divider between rows, vertical divider between columns. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: One category expanded with compact supporting grid
variants.layout: Left 55%: hero quadrant with expanded items (icon + name + full description + metric). Right 45%: 3 compact quadrants stacked. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Hierarchical objectives — campaign goals feed intermediate goals feed an apex objective. Classic 3→2→1 convergence tree for strategy alignment.

signals: prompt describes objectives at multiple levels that feed into a single goal
has 'business objectives', 'campaign goals', 'converge', 'feed into', 'build toward'
3-tier hierarchy: foundational actions → intermediate goals → apex objective
the relationship between levels is the deliverable, not just a list of goals

emphasis_question.prompt: How should the reader follow the hierarchy?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'build toward', 'contribute to', 'feed into' → aspiration. If 'break down', 'decompose', 'consists of', 'accountability' → decomposition.

options.label: Build up
options.description: Bottom-up pyramid — objectives converge upward toward the apex goal (aspirational energy)

options.label: Break down
options.description: Top-down bracket — apex goal decomposes downward into supporting objectives (accountability chain)

variants.name: Bottom-up pyramid with curved arrow connectors
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with strategist claim. 3-tier pyramid: 3 leaf nodes (bordered pills) at bottom → 2 mid nodes (brand-blue pills) in center → 1 apex node (orange pill) at top. Curved SVG arrows connect upward. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Top-down org-chart with bracket connectors
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with strategist claim. 3-tier bracket tree: 3 leaf nodes (bordered pills) at top → 2 mid nodes (brand-blue pills) in center → 1 apex node (orange pill) at bottom. Straight bracket-style SVG connectors flow downward. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Project timeline with explicit dates, phase categories, and dated sub-tasks. Implementation plans, migration roadmaps, engagement timelines, rollout schedules.

match.disambiguate_rule: Use implementation-timeline when the prompt has EXPLICIT DATES or date ranges tied to deliverables. Use process-flow when the prompt describes abstract stages, phases, or steps without calendar dates.
signals: prompt describes a project plan with specific dates or date ranges
has 'timeline', 'roadmap', 'implementation plan', 'schedule', 'milestones'
work is organized into phases or categories each with their own dates
sub-tasks or deliverables are tied to specific dates or weeks

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the timeline emphasize?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'show overlap' or 'parallel workstreams' → gantt. If 'what happens when' or 'phase by phase' → phases. If 'key dates' or 'milestones' → hybrid.

options.label: Key milestones
options.description: Hero the critical dates on a timeline rail, with phase detail cards below

options.label: Duration & overlap
options.description: Horizontal swim lanes showing how long each workstream runs and where they overlap

options.label: What happens when
options.description: Vertical stacked phase blocks with specific dated deliverables in each

variants.name: Timeline rail + phase detail cards
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with headline. Horizontal timeline bar with progress fill and 3-5 milestone dots (done/current/upcoming). Below: 3-4 phase cards in a row, each with colored top border, category title, date range, and 2-4 dated sub-items with optional status chips. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Swim lane bars with overlap indicators
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with headline. Horizontal date axis at top. Category swim lanes as horizontal bars with date-range fills. Overlap zones highlighted. Milestone diamonds on the axis. Legend + summary at bottom.

variants.name: Vertical phase blocks with dated deliverables
variants.layout: Full-width. Header with headline. Stacked vertical phase blocks (full-width), each with phase header (title + date range + duration badge) and 2-4 dated deliverable rows. Phase connector arrows between blocks. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Company financial progress — multi-metric health check, headline summary, or plan-vs-actual variance. Quarterly results, annual reviews, P&L analysis.

signals: prompt reviews financial performance across multiple metrics
has 'financial review', 'quarterly results', 'P&L', 'financial progress', 'how did we perform'
multiple financial KPIs with period-over-period changes or budget comparisons

emphasis_question.prompt: What kind of financial review is this?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'scorecard' or 'how are we doing' or 'financial health' → scorecard. If 'top line' or 'headline' or 'summary for leadership' → headline. If 'vs budget' or 'vs plan' or 'vs forecast' or 'variance' → variance.

options.label: Full scorecard
options.description: Multi-metric dashboard — 4-6 KPIs with trend sparklines + narrative findings

options.label: Headline summary
options.description: Hero number + supporting metrics + narrative — for leadership briefings

options.label: Budget vs actual
options.description: Variance table + gap callouts + remediation — for plan-to-actual analysis

variants.name: Multi-metric scorecard with trend sparklines
variants.layout: Full-width. 2×3 KPI grid (value + delta chip + label + 4-bar sparkline). Below: 3 horizontal finding cards. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Hero stat + supporting metrics + narrative
variants.layout: Full-width. Hero stat panel (64px value + delta + context). Stat row (3-4 supporting metrics). Narrative block. Action strip at bottom.

variants.name: Budget vs actual table with gap callouts
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: P&L variance table (7 rows + totals, color-coded variance cells). Right: gap callouts (magnitude + explanation) + remediation actions. Summary bar at bottom.

families.description: Internal rollout or launch update — what's done, what's next, who's involved, timeline milestones. Training rollouts, product launches, adoption tracking.

signals: prompt announces a launch, rollout, or program update with status tracking
has 'launching', 'rollout', 'training complete', 'up next', 'progress toward'
tracks completion status (done/pending) AND scope (participants, clients, teams)
internal audience — team updates, not external product marketing

emphasis_question.prompt: What's the main message — status, scope, or timeline?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on 'what's done vs what's next' → balanced. If 'how many / who's adopted' → adoption. If 'key dates' → timeline.

options.label: Status + scope
options.description: Two-zone view — left shows what's done/next, right shows who/what is in scope

options.label: Adoption metrics
options.description: Progress bars and counts are the hero — status details are supporting

options.label: Timeline-forward
options.description: Key dates and milestones dominate — status and scope are compact context

variants.name: Two-zone status + detail with progress bars
variants.layout: Full-width. Header. Two-zone body: left status panel (completed group + upcoming group) | right detail panel (table or list). Progress bars below. Optional milestone strip. Footer.

families.description: Named initiative cards with owners — 3-5 workstreams each with a responsible person and their deliverables. The bread-and-butter leadership alignment slide.

signals: prompt lists 3-5 initiatives or workstreams each with a named owner/leader
has person names paired with responsibilities or deliverables
internal audience — team structure, accountability, priorities
items are peer workstreams, not sequential phases

emphasis_question.prompt: How should the initiatives relate to each other?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If all initiatives are equally important → balanced. If one initiative is the priority → focal. If there's a status dimension (new vs established) → status.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: All initiative cards shown at the same size — reader scans the full portfolio

options.label: One leads
options.description: One initiative is expanded as the hero — the others are compact supporting cards

options.label: Status-tagged
options.description: Cards carry status badges (new, pilot, established) — reader sees maturity mix

variants.name: KPI strip + owner card row
variants.layout: Full-width stacked. Optional KPI strip (dark primary). 3-5 equal-width owner cards in a row (title + name + role + responsibilities). Summary bar. Footer.
